## 7.1 Fern Diseases: Rust, Puccinia asparagi, Purple Spot, Stemphylium vesicarium, and other fern diseases

**Time for concern:** Late spring through end of season.

**Key characteristics: Rust:** red or brown elongated spots appear on spears or ferns. Ferns may prematurely yellow and brown. Purple spot: occurs on both ferns and spears. On spears lesions are slightly sunken and dark purplish. On ferns the lesions are slightly darker with a purplish-red margin. When disease is severe, needles will drop, leading to defoliation of the fern. When these diseases affect marketability of spears, fungicides need to be applied to ferns for control. See Michigan State Extension Bulletin E3219, [Disease and Insect Pests of Asparagus.](https://www.canr.msu.edu/uploads/resources/pdfs/Disease_and_Insect_Pests_of_Asparagus_(E3219).pdf)

### 7.2 Fusarium Root Rot and Fusarium Crown Rot, Fusarium spp.

**Time for concern:** Planting through life of bed.

**Key characteristics:** Fusarium causes weak, spindly spear production and overall reduced vigor over time. Feeder roots become rotted and discolored. Affected crowns show reddish brown discoloration when cut. If asparagus beds are experiencing dieback from Fusarium, you may want to investigate whether asparagus miner (Section 8.2) is part of the problem. See Michigan State Extension Bulletin E3219, [Disease and Insect Pests of Asparagus](https://www.canr.msu.edu/uploads/resources/pdfs/Disease_and_Insect_Pests_of_Asparagus_(E3219).pdf).

### 7.3 Phytophthora Spear and Crown Rot, Phytophthora spp.

**Time for concern**: This disease is currently not a problem in New York State, but its potential for occurring on Long Island is high.

**Key characteristics:** Infected spears show gray-beige to brown lesions slightly above or just below the soil line. The decay is odorless unless invaded by saprophytic bacteria. See description in Michigan State University Bulletin E3219: [Disease and insect pests of asparagus](https://www.canr.msu.edu/uploads/resources/pdfs/Disease_and_Insect_Pests_of_Asparagus_(E3219).pdf).
